transcript: I didn't think it was possible to pull off such a fresh and fun take on The Pirates of Penzance until I saw this production at Roundabout last night. This new version of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera kind of has no business being as good as it is. It's framed like a show within a show, with Gilbert Sullivan as characters bringing it to New Orleans. We get bright and colorful costumes, a consolidated libretto, and some completely new and jazzy orchestrations. This production brings out the silliness of the story, which has always been a bunch of nonsense about pirates and maidens, but there's a lot of attention paid to learning each and every joke here, many of which are intentionally corny or punny. Combined with some really fun ensemble numbers, particularly one delightful sequence involving washboards, this production maintains that vital buoyancy that most good musical comedies have. Act 2 doesn't hit quite as hard as Act 1, as it has fewer opportunities to lean into the New Orleans concept, and the marchy score eventually gets a little tedious, but these are pretty minor complaints, all things considered. This won't change your life or anything like that, but it's a well-conceived production that has the fun, the funny, and some great performances, especially from David Hyde Pierce, Ramin Karimloo, and Jinkx Monsoon, who are all perfectly cast. Pirates! The Penzance Musical is running on Broadway through July. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
